strengths: Addresses an important practical constraint: unlearning using only the pretrained model and forgetting data. The target-versus-nontarget input-sensitivity objective is an interesting refinement of sensitivity-based unlearning.

Strong full-class and subclass results. MU-Mis achieves average accuracy gaps from retraining of 0.07 on CIFAR-100 and 0.15 on Tiny ImageNet, substantially outperforming several retained-data-free baselines.
Demonstrates useful efficiency gains: Tiny ImageNet unlearning takes 83 seconds versus 2,630 seconds for SalUn, with a small difference in average accuracy gap.

The evaluation includes six datasets, multiple architectures, sequential deletion, objective ablations, and five-trial summaries. Pseudocode, experimental configurations, and a public code link support reproducibility.
weaknesses: The central theoretical connection is not established. Differentiating the training algorithm with respect to an example measures input perturbation, rather than deletion influence. Section 3.2 drops probability and training-trajectory derivative terms without error control. Appendix D also does not establish that the summed cross-sample residual is negligible; ReLU activation alone cannot justify this assumption.

The derivations contain concrete mathematical errors. Section 3.2 reverses the cross-entropy logit-gradient sign: it should be p minus the one-hot label. Equation (A7) omits derivatives of the softmax probabilities. Consequently, its expression predicts zero loss curvature for affine logits, although softmax cross-entropy generally has positive curvature. These errors weaken the claimed theoretical grounding.

Utility preservation and superiority claims exceed the results. In Table A8, MU-Mis has an average gap of 19.85 versus RUM's 0.84, with test accuracy 57.37% versus retraining's 84.45%. Table A16 shows substantial failures on highly memorized examples. Even among retained-data-free methods, Table A7 reports a worse SVHN average gap than NG, RL, and JiT, contradicting the claimed superiority across all scenarios.

The privacy interpretation is insufficiently justified. MIA-Entropy reports the fraction of forgotten examples classified as members; minimizing this quantity does not establish indistinguishability from retraining. For CIFAR-20 Sea, MU-Mis scores 1.25 versus retraining's 51.61, a substantial distributional discrepancy. The additional SCRUB-LiRA evaluation is useful, but attack configuration and calibration details are insufficient to support the broad privacy claims.

The practical calibration protocol remains unclear. Stopping thresholds vary from 0.68 to 3.0 and reach 10 during sequential deletion, while important experiments use an additional reweighting factor of 80 absent from Algorithm 1. The paper does not explain how these choices are selected without retained-data validation or a retrained oracle. Sensitivity analysis over thresholds 0.7–1.0 on one task does not resolve this concern.

Important numerical results require reconciliation. Under Equation (A4), Table A8's pretrained KL values require the forgetting subset to have weight at most 6.7%, whereas its MU-Mis values require at least 78.4%; these cannot describe the same partition. Tables A7 and A11 also report unexplained MIA-Entropy differences, 33.04 versus 83.34, for CIFAR-10 10% deletion. These inconsistencies undermine confidence in the distributional and privacy evidence.
